title: 'Time traveler' in painting from 1937 seen with something very unexpected
excerpt: A painting titled Mr Pynchon and the Settling of Springfield, crafted by Italian artist Umberto Romano in 1937, has sparked time travel conspiracy theories after a Native American figure was spotted holding a mysterious object
content:
A painting titled Mr Pynchon and the Settling of Springfield, crafted by Italian artist Umberto Romano in 1937, has sparked time travel conspiracy theories after a Native American figure was spotted holding a mysterious object

02:00 ET, 05 Sep 2026Updated 04:49 ET, 05 Sep 2026

Conspiracy theorists are convinced that a nearly century-old painting featuring a Native American figure holding what appears to be a 'smartphone' is definitive proof that time travel is real.

‌

The piece, Mr Pynchon and the Settling of Springfield, was created by Italian painter Umberto Romano in 1937 and portrays colonists making their way into the Massachusetts settlement during the 1620s.

An indigenous person can be spotted gripping a compact, dark rectangular object that looks remarkably similar to an iPhone, gazing down at it, almost as if he's taking a selfie.

This mysterious object has left observers scratching their heads, with several people jumping to the theory that it could indicate time travel, given that iPhones didn't hit the market until 2007.

However, Brian Anderson, in his analysis for Motherboard, concluded that the device is almost certainly a mirror, reports the Daily Star.

‌

Mr Anderson explained: "There's reason to believe, then, that what the man is examining is not an Indigenous object, but rather of European origin, like mirrors, which were presented often in such exchanges," he wrote.

"The way the man holds it up, if indeed he's looking at his own face reflecting back at him, would certainly make sense."

‌

Yet this is not the first instance of a 'smartphone' being depicted in historical art predating the technology's invention.

Time-travel believers doubled down on their hypothesis after a woman was caught apparently holding a 'mobile phone' in the background of a 1928 Charlie Chaplin film. The grainy monochrome clip of the supposed 'time traveller' comes from the silent film legend's movie, The Circus.

In the sequence, a woman wearing a black top hat and white gloves appears to be walking in the background, holding what appears to be a device close to her face, leading many observers to claim she's using a mobile phone.

‌

Handheld mobile phones didn't hit the market until the 1980s, approximately 50 years after the Charlie Chaplin film premiered. Irish director George Clarke unearthed the 'time traveller' footage from the 1928 production in 2010, subsequently sharing his discovery on his YouTube platform.

In the video, which has accumulated nearly seven million views, the director explained: "If you look carefully, she's talking on a thin, black device that is held to her ear. If you notice, the knuckles are also bent in the flat shape of a phone.

"The phone is to the ear. It's not an ear trumpet. It is not an AM/FM radio, obviously, because it's 1928. Technically, there's nothing that can explain what is in her hand... It's clear she's talking. She's on her own. She's talking into the device."

Days after George's YouTube post went live, conspiracy theorists began circulating their explanations for the 'time traveller' footage. Some suggested the woman was merely shielding her face from the sun, while others maintained she was simply holding her ear.

Despite the online frenzy, the Daily News was quick to shut down the speculation, stating that "while this fantastical theory is fun to ponder, in all likelihood the woman is actually using a hearing aid."
